name: Pacioli’s printed account of Venetian double-entry
description: Pacioli’s 1494 Summa described the double-entry bookkeeping used by Venetian merchants in Italian, making a practical accounting method available to readers of the printed book.

date.basis: The publication date of the Summa, not the invention date of double-entry.

events.statement: Pacioli published a description of Venetian double-entry accounting.
events.caveats: The merchants’ method predated the publication; this is a record of codification, not the invention of bookkeeping. The extent of readership and actual use by different groups requires further evidence.

evidence.supports: Pacioli published a description of Venetian double-entry accounting.
Identifies Pacioli as author and Paganino de Paganini as the Venice printer in 1494.

events.scope: Printed 1494 treatment of Venetian commercial accounting, not the earlier invention of the method.

contributions.resource: Wrote the Summa and its treatment of bookkeeping.

evidence.supports: Identifies Pacioli as author and the accounting section.
Identifies Paganino de Paganini as the printer.

earliest_record.rationale: The publication date of the Summa, not the invention date of double-entry. Earliest record means earliest currently established for this scoped case, not global priority.

caveats: The merchants’ method predated the publication; this is a record of codification, not the invention of bookkeeping. The extent of readership and actual use by different groups requires further evidence.
